_about: Build review of every finding confirmed by both models, done by reading the policy text during development (2026-10-28). verdict: upheld (the policy as written says this), qualified (true as written, with a caveat a reader needs), rejected (the policy says otherwise; both models missed it). 'match' picks the finding by a phrase from its summary.

reviews.note: Charity is limited to uninsured or underinsured patients; Colorado HDC must screen an insured patient who asks.
The policy requires the date of service to be within 181 days of applying, with no extra window after an insurance adjustment.
181 days from service can end before 240 days after the first bill when insurance delays the bill.
ECAs no sooner than 120 days after the first statement; statements may start on day 46.
ECAs not until at least 120 days after the first post-discharge statement; no 182-day floor stated.
Assistance is for people who are uninsured or underinsured.
Charity care is for qualified patients who are uninsured or underinsured.
A band gap: the policy's bands end at 225% and restart at 226%. Likely a rounding convention, not an intended exclusion.
Residency within an Intermountain service area is required for non-emergent services.
Eligibility is considered for uninsured or underinsured individuals.
Applications are due within 45 days of service (or 45 days after an insurance payment or Medicaid denial); Colorado allows at least 181 days.
The policy also allows 45 days from the date of primary insurance payment, which meets Colorado's insured-patient window. Both models missed that option.
Payment plans must be at least $25 a month; for very low incomes that exceeds 4% of monthly income. Accounts must also be paid within 24 months.
This is a plain-language summary; it also offers help 'if it would be a financial hardship to pay', which may cover insured patients.
The sliding scale stops at 200%, but the policy says discounts 'could include the HDC program' without describing it.
Income-based assistance requires the patient to be uninsured or under-insured (out-of-pocket costs exceed ability to pay).
A band gap: 100% at 250% or less, discounts 'between 251% and 400%'. Likely a rounding convention.
